text:
Erin (VP Eng): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — thanks for the great Q&A. Two asks to keep this thread tight: 1) can leads clarify prioritization between kernel-v5 latency work vs batching/caching improvements? 2) any timeline or rollout impacts for Dedicated/Private customers? Please reply with short bullets. -Erin

Devon (Runtime Lead): Short answer: kernel-v5 is prioritized for tail-latency wins on long-context workloads; batching/caching work yields better unit-cost wins for short/interactive workloads. Both proceed in parallel but with different owners.

Priya (Infra PM): For Dedicated/Private: no SLA changes planned. We'll do controlled canaries and opt-in upgrades for private deployments; customers can delay rollouts.

Kai (Staff Engineer): Technical clarifications: kernel-v5 bundles two big changes — (A) attention reorder for improved memory locality and (B) fused rotary + QKV fast path for RTX/AMX. Batching/caching changes are scheduler/policy-driven: smarter prefix reuse + prefetch heuristics. Not all models will see identical improvements.

Devon (Runtime Lead): Prioritization bullets:
- Sprint 1-2: kernel-v5 correctness, tests, microbenchmarks.
- Sprint 3: large perf patches + canary infra.
- Sprint 4: stabilization + rollout.
Batching/caching roadmap: continuous improvements, policy engine revamp across 3 sprints, with incremental deployments.

Erin (VP Eng): Sounds reasonable. Major risks? rollback strategy?

Devon (Runtime Lead): Risks: GPU memory fragmentation, quantization path edge cases, and rare KV-cache eviction races. Rollback: automatic fallback to v4 kernels and model-variant routing; canaries + health gates. Canary window target: 48-72h.

Priya (Infra PM): Ops details: we'll create canary channels, tag impacted customers, and publish a short runbook. We'll monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rates.

ops-bot: Canary run created: #canary-kernel-v5-241234. Auto-rollback configured: trigger if p50 latency > baseline +20% or error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m.

Kai (Staff Engineer): Batching note: short-request-heavy services need special handling. If your model is dominated by <64-token requests, flag it. Aggressive batching may increase tail latency for some user patterns. Example opt-in config: 
```json
{"batching": {"mode": "aggressive", "max_batch_ms": 15}}
```

Devon (Runtime Lead): Docs/RFC plan: I'll post an RFC in #eng-runtime tomorrow with end-to-end benchmarks (p50/p95/p99), a list of models we tested, and 'what to expect' migration notes.

Erin (VP Eng): Action items: Devon - post RFC + benchmarks; Priya - publish canary runbook + channel; Kai - compile a list of short-request models and DM product owners. We'll do a 30-min follow-up this Friday. :thumbsup: Keep updates concise here.

Devon (Runtime Lead): Noted, will post link when ready.

Priya (Infra PM): I'll drop the runbook + canary link this afternoon.

Kai (Staff Engineer): I'll assemble the model list and start outreach.

Erin (VP Eng): Thanks all. If you have one-sentence blockers call them out now, otherwise let's keep everything in the follow-up thread. End.
